purpose: Bounded Fair Work Ombudsman record connecting a migrant worker's zero-wage cashback exposure to institutional investigation, full reported back-pay, and an open durable-recovery endpoint.

events.geography: Sydney, Australia; Federal Circuit and Family Court; temporary graduate visa holder
events.date_precision: official Fair Work Ombudsman penalty release date; employment ran July 2019 to December 2020
events.denominator: One publicly identified adjudicated worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Ombudsman penalty follow-up release
events.missingness: Worker identity beyond the public case, household effects, effort and time spent seeking help, payment instrument, net receipt timing, adequacy, later employment, trust, recurrence, health, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: A Nepalese migrant worker employed part-time as an assistant accountant was unpaid for roughly the first ten weeks and was then required to transfer money to accounts controlled by the owner so the company could return part of it as wages and satisfy tax and superannuation obligations; the official release reports total underpayment of $40,164.49
events.alternatives_before_action: The public record does not report alternative employment, household buffers, bargaining alternatives, or non-use before the worker requested Fair Work Ombudsman assistance
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The cashback scheme left the worker with no wages to keep for work performed and imposed transfer, documentation, and visa-linked vulnerability risks; the release says the conduct was deliberate
events.choice_or_response: The worker lodged a request for assistance; the Fair Work Ombudsman investigated and litigated; the Court imposed penalties after admissions and findings of deliberate contraventions
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer and owner controlled payroll, bank transfers, records, and the employment relationship; the worker controlled the request for assistance; the Ombudsman and Court controlled investigation, litigation, and penalty routes
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Federal Circuit and Family Court imposed $148,000 against Innovative Associates and $29,000 against its owner; the official release reports that the company back-paid the worker in full
events.remedy_receipt: The Fair Work Ombudsman reports full back-payment of the $40,164.49 underpayment, but the public record does not provide a worker-signed receipt, transfer date, net amount, or adequacy assessment
events.durability_followup: The public follow-up ends at reported full back-pay and penalties; later work, household security, trust, recurrence, health, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Reported full back-pay followed by court penalties for the company and owner
events.protected_outcome: The institutional route recognized the worker's wage entitlement and reports restoring the withheld monetary amount; durable safety, bargaining power, and future employment protection are not verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: The worker lost usable wage income during employment and carried the exposure, delay, documentation, and help-seeking burden before the reported remedy
events.cost_risk_transfer: The employer shifted wage, liquidity, and compliance risk onto a temporary-visa worker; investigation, litigation, and penalties transferred formal legal risk back to the firm and owner
events.later_outcome: The official institution reports full back-pay and penalties, but no later lived-recovery endpoint is public
events.meaning_and_attribution: The Court and Ombudsman attribute the conduct to deliberate exploitation and an unlawful cashback scheme; no worker-reported trust or meaning measure is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: Public enforcement and penalty are observed; the release encourages visa holders and other employees to seek assistance, but no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: A public enforcement record can report full monetary back-pay for a vulnerable worker while leaving payment timing, adequacy, safety, trust, and future work unobserved
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release dated 2026-09-01, https://www.fairwork.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/2026-media-releases/september-2026/20260901-innovative-associates-penalty-media-release; court findings and reported full back-pay are institutionally reported, not independently audited here

arrows.from: unlawful cashback scheme and zero usable wages
arrows.to: worker request for Fair Work Ombudsman assistance
arrows.evidence: The official release states that the Ombudsman investigated after the worker lodged a request for assistance
arrows.counterexample: A request for help does not establish that other exposed workers can reach or safely use the same route
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker effort, delay, fear, representation, and alternative routes

arrows.evidence: The release reports $177,000 in penalties and says the company back-paid the worker in full
arrows.counterexample: Institutional reporting is not an independently verified payment instrument or adequacy assessment
arrows.remaining_gap: Transfer timing, net receipt, worker confirmation, adequacy, and residual loss

arrows.to: durable security, trust, later work, or exit
arrows.evidence: The official follow-up ends after reporting full back-pay and penalties
arrows.counterexample: Monetary restoration can coexist with unresolved safety, visa, household, trust, and employment consequences
arrows.remaining_gap: Later work, household recovery, trust, recurrence, health, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes a reported full-back-pay endpoint for one vulnerable migrant worker. It does not establish independently verified receipt, adequacy, durable recovery, prevalence, or a general enforcement success rate.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, payroll, bank, visa, or restricted data is retained; only bounded official summary fields and explicitly open downstream arrows are represented.
